paper.title: Exploring Facets of Language Generation in the Limit
paper.summary: Develops nonuniform generation and its membership-query lower bound, introduces exhaustive generation and its weak-Angluin characterization, and characterizes uniform generation with target feedback by GF dimension. The registered surface separates semantic theorem coverage from randomized, oracle-realization, relative-computability, and quantitative-rate frontiers.

formalization_scope.summary: Of nineteen paper-owned numbered-result cards, fifteen have full Lean coverage, three are partial, and one has no coverage. Proposition 6.2 has its semantic strong-oracle core but no typed oracle-relative realization, Proposition 6.3 has an explicit membership-query construction but no relative-computability certificate for the dependent algorithm, and Example 11 lacks a named endpoint for its asymptotic sweep thresholds. Randomized Corollary 5.1 is unformalized.
specializations: Paper-facing generation theorems expose Section 2's standing infinite-language assumption through UUS; Theorems 2 and 7 state infinitude on both languages directly.

Theorem 6 is stronger than its printed exact-enumeration statement: Lean proves the threshold guarantee for every target-contained stream once enough distinct examples have appeared, over an arbitrary infinite universe.
Theorems 5, Proposition 6.1, Proposition 7.1, and Lemmas 7.2--7.3 permit arbitrary language classes over their stated universes rather than retaining the paper's countable-class context.
Proposition 7.1 represents equality of possibly unbounded dimensions by equivalence at every positive finite level, avoiding an auxiliary extended-natural value.
Example 10 uses a canonical explicit partition, and Claim 5.2 uses the Nat reencoding of Example 9's integer co-singleton class.
Except for Theorem 7's explicit Mathlib Computable machine interface and Proposition 6.3's computable tell-tale emitter hypothesis, the registered generators are semantic and generally noncomputable.
gaps: No randomized exhaustive-generation or probability framework formalizes Corollary 5.1.
Proposition 6.2 does not expose the finite-difference and subset oracles as a typed relative implementation interface.
Proposition 6.3 does not certify the constructed noncomputable dependent algorithm as computable relative to the membership oracle.
Example 11's O(|i|) and O(max{|i|,|j|}) language-dependent sweep thresholds are used informally and in proof-local choices but are not stated by a public Lean declaration.

Only Overview Theorems 1--4 have named human statement-correspondence review; all other source correspondence, all proof bodies, and the completion-driven Theorem 7 repair remain outside that human scope.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Nineteen paper-owned numbered-result cards: Overview Theorems 1--5; detailed Theorems 6--7; Corollary 5.1; Example 9; Claim 5.2; Proposition 5.3; Propositions 6.1--6.3; Example 10; Proposition 7.1; Lemmas 7.2--7.3; and Example 11. The Section 5.1 restatement of Theorem 3 is grouped with its overview statement, and Example 11's quantitative sweep-rate sentence is retained as a component of that example.
exclusions: Definitions 1--11, Remarks 1--6, quoted prior-work and open-question statements, algorithms as standalone claims, unnumbered discussion, and proof-only intermediates do not receive separate cards.
Theorem 8 is excluded because the paper explicitly recalls Angluin 1980 Theorem 1; its canonical ownership and effective formalization are P00A, not P04.
The duplicate Section 5.1 presentation of Theorem 3 does not receive a second card.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means complete for this nineteen-card custom numbered-result scope, not for every definition or informal sentence in arXiv v2. The PDF title page is dated 25 December 2024, while the retained source-edition date is the arXiv v2 version date, 24 December 2024; both identify the same SHA-pinned file.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: The twenty-five canonical paper-facing or example-headline declarations directly linked to the nineteen claims in this custom source scope.
exclusions: Definitions, constructors, private proof lemmas, countability and UUS helpers, and implementation internals not needed as canonical claim endpoints.

Duplicate internal results such as theorem_seven, theorem4_exhaustive_generation_characterization, theorem5_uniform_feedback_characterization, nonuniform_upper_bound, parameterized Example 10 helpers, and nonuniform_upper_bound_no_repetition are excluded when a listed wrapper or headline endpoint exposes the source claim.
P02, P03, and P05 bridge declarations, P02 closure results reused inside proofs, and the recalled P00A Angluin theorem are cross-paper reuse or discoverability, not duplicate P04 coverage links.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: All twenty-five proposed endpoints compile and depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The generated audit should remain the complete mechanical check; the existing hand-maintained Audit.lean covers only a selected subset.

claims.title: Every countable collection is nonuniformly generatable
claims.statement_summary: Every countably indexed collection of infinite languages over the fixed countable string universe admits one generator whose distinct-sample threshold may depend on the target language.

formalization.notes: The source's standing infinitude assumption is explicit as UUS over the family range.

relations.notes: Theorem 6 supplies the quantitative generator bound used to prove Theorem 1.

claims.statement_summary: No single deterministic algorithm using only membership queries can nonuniformly generate for every countable collection; the paper proves the stronger obstruction already for genuine two-language collections.

source_assessment.notes: The overview statement is sound, but its detailed Theorem 7 proof is repaired in Lean rather than mirrored literally.

claims.title: A countable regular class can fail exhaustive generation
claims.statement_summary: There exists a countable class of infinite regular languages over a finite alphabet that cannot be exhaustively generated in the limit.

source_refs.locator: Theorem 3, overview statement and Section 5.1 restatement

formalization.notes: Lean packages countability, UUS, regularity, and non-generatability in one existential witness.

lean_links.notes: Uses an explicit signed-unary regular-ray witness over List Bool.

relations.notes: The concrete regular witness violates Weak Angluin existence, so Proposition 6.1 rules out exhaustive generation.

Generated audit for the existential theorem wrapper.

claims.title: Exhaustive generation is characterized by Weak Angluin existence
claims.statement_summary: A countably indexed collection of infinite languages is exhaustively generatable if and only if every language has a finite weak Angluin tell-tale whose proper sublanguages omit only finitely many target words.

formalization.notes: The headline is semantic; oracle realization boundaries are represented on the Proposition 6.2 and 6.3 cards.

lean_links.notes: Explicit UUS exposes the paper's standing infinite-language assumption.

relations.notes: Proposition 6.1 proves the necessary direction.
Proposition 6.2 proves the semantic sufficient direction.
Both use a weak-Angluin predicate, but the P04-to-P05 bridge does not establish identity of the two papers' source exhaustive-generation interfaces.

audit_refs.scope: Named-result human statement correspondence for the semantic headline only; oracle realization is outside scope.
Generated audit for the characterization wrapper.

claims.title: Uniform feedback generation is characterized by finite GF dimension
claims.statement_summary: A class of infinite languages over a countable universe is uniformly generatable with target-membership feedback if and only if its GF dimension is finite.

formalization.notes: Lean strengthens the source-context reading by dropping countability of the language class itself.

lean_links.notes: Explicit UUS retains the standing infinite-language assumption.

relations.notes: Lemma 7.2 proves sufficiency.

claims.title: The greedy generator has an explicit nonuniform sample threshold
claims.statement_summary: For target L_i, the greedy generator is correct and fresh after the distinct sample has size at least max{i in one-based indexing, m_C(L_i)+1}.

formalization.notes: The wrapper is stronger than the source: it needs only target containment of the stream, not an exhaustive presentation.

lean_links.notes: Lean's zero-based index is shifted by i+1 to match the paper's one-based threshold.

relations.notes: The pointwise bound yields the target-dependent threshold in Theorem 1.

claims.title: No universal computable adaptive membership-query generator exists even for two languages
claims.statement_summary: No single computable deterministic adaptive membership-query machine terminates each round and satisfies target-dependent nonuniform freshness guarantees for every genuine pair of distinct infinite languages.

source_assessment.notes: The printed proof's infinite-loop discussion does not justify that infinitely many distinct common words are discovered. Lean proves the same statement by a completion-driven diagonal, using universality to force finite termination on every temporary infinite completion.

formalization.notes: The repaired proof preserves the exact source claim and exposes the operational query/termination model.

lean_links.notes: TheoremSevenStatement explicitly models finite answered-query traces and possible nontermination.

relations.notes: The size-two obstruction is stronger than the overview all-countable-collections impossibility.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for detailed Theorem 7. The Human ledger explicitly excludes this detailed theorem and proof repair.

claims.title: Randomization does not evade the exhaustive-generation lower bound
claims.statement_summary: For the Theorem 3 class, no randomized algorithm can make both eventual finite future error and full exhaustive coverage hold with probability greater than one half at every sufficiently late time.

source_assessment.notes: The proof's reference to Theorem 8 is an evident cross-reference typo for Theorem 3.

formalization.notes: P04 Lean contains no randomized exhaustive algorithm, probability distribution, or greater-than-one-half joint-event interface.

relations.notes: The source modifies the deterministic Theorem 3 diagonal by intersecting two probability-greater-than-one-half events.

claims.title: A non-identifiable co-singleton class is exhaustively generatable
claims.statement_summary: The integer class consisting of the whole universe and all co-singletons has no finite tell-tale for the whole universe, hence is not identifiable by the recalled Angluin theorem, yet an input-oblivious integer sweep exhaustively generates it.

formalization.notes: The native P04 obstruction is stronger than failure of effective identification; the general recalled characterization remains owned by P00A.

components.summary: No finite subset of the whole integer universe is an Angluin tell-tale against all co-singletons.
The same class is exhaustively generated by the explicit integer sweep.

lean_links.notes: This is the exact source obstruction used before invoking recalled Theorem 8.
The generate-only range is the future tail of a fixed bijective integer sweep.

relations.notes: The source invokes recalled Theorem 8, Angluin's effective characterization, to turn tell-tale failure into non-identifiability; that prior theorem is not duplicated as P04 coverage.
Claim 5.2 uses the Nat-reencoded co-singleton family from this example.

claims.statement_summary: Every exhaustively generatable class of infinite languages over a countable universe satisfies Weak Angluin's Condition with Existence.

claims.title: Computably enumerated weak tell-tales suffice using membership queries
claims.statement_summary: If one total computable stage procedure uniformly enumerates finite weak tell-tales, an exhaustive generator can select a safe language using only membership queries to the indexed family.

claims.title: Feedback enables uniform generation for a class with infinite closure dimension
claims.statement_summary: A canonical countable class built from a growing partition has infinite ordinary closure dimension and is not uniformly generatable without feedback, but a fixed target-membership query separates its even and odd language branches and yields uniform generation with feedback.

formalization.notes: Lean uses a canonical explicit partition satisfying the source data.

The class is not uniformly generatable without target feedback.
One fixed target-membership query per round yields a uniform feedback generator.

The strategy always queries -2, whose answer selects the even or odd negative core.

claims.title: GnF dimension equals closure dimension

formalization.notes: Level-by-level positive equivalence exactly captures both finite equality and simultaneous unboundedness without defining an extended-natural supremum.

claims.title: A co-singleton/co-doubleton class is nonuniform but not uniform even with feedback
